original.target_description: Experiment 1: Need for Cognition × Argument Quality interaction on mean five-item message evaluation

n.quote: One hundred fourteen undergraduates (S3 men and 61 women) ultimately participated
n.exclusions: Recruited from upper/lower thirds of need for cognition scores; middle third not recruited. No analytic exclusions reported.

es.quote: Need for Cognition X Argument Quality interaction, F(l, 110) = 22.45, p< .001

p.quote: Need for Cognition X Argument Quality interaction, F(l, 110) = 22.45, p< .001

replication.target_description: Study 8/4.8: Condition × continuous need for cognition interaction predicting five-item argument-quality evaluation; in-lab aggregate

n.sample_role: participants included in target aggregate analysis
n.exclusions: Roughly 200 participants received arguments for the wrong university and were removed (footnote 9).

reported_success.quote: Participants’ need for cognition did not qualify the effect of argument quality on persuasion.

notes: Target is the interaction, not the strong-versus-weak main effect. Replication uses continuous need for cognition; original used upper/lower thirds. Footnote 11 also reports the restricted-thirds interaction, F(1, 1,563) = 1.102, p = .294, ηp² = 0.0007; this is a distinct secondary test. Original reports F rather than standardized effect size; no conversion performed. OCR renders 53 men as S3.
